text: If every wheel on Earth vanished tonight, you wouldn't make it to work tomorrow... and that's the least of your problems.
First, every car, bus and train drops straight onto its axles, freezing every highway into one giant parking lot.
But it's not just vehicles. Inside your watch, your engine, and every power plant, gears are just wheels with teeth.
So the turbines stop spinning, and the power grid collapses. Lights out, across the entire planet.
Without trucks, supermarket shelves would be empty in about three days, because food simply can't move fast enough.
Planes are grounded too. No landing gear to take off, and no spinning turbines inside the jet engines.
So we'd go back to moving heavy things the ancient way: dragging them on sledges with ropes and muscle.
But here's the crazy part. Humans lived for hundreds of thousands of years without the wheel. It was only invented about 5,500 years ago... and not for carts.
It was for making pottery. Which means if wheels disappeared, someone would probably reinvent them within a week.
Because the wheel isn't just an invention. It's the thing quietly holding the modern world together.
